question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the following sentence:

 

The ______ addressed the students during the morning assembly.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Principal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Principal means the head of a school or institution; also, main or most important. (प्रधानाचार्य / मुख्य)
◦ Example: She was appointed as the principal of the college last year.

 

• The sentence is correctly completed with Principal: "The Principal addressed the students during the morning assembly."

 

• Memory trick: a school Principal is your pal, while a Principle is a rule you follow — matching the last three letters helps you remember which is which.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Principle (सिद्धांत): a fundamental truth or rule that guides behaviour.

 

• Option 3: Principally (मुख्यतः): mainly or chiefly; for the most part.

 

• Option 4: Principality (रियासत): a state or territory ruled by a prince.

 

NOTE

 

• Other frequently confused pairs tested by SSC: Stationary/Stationery, Complement/Compliment, and Council/Counsel.

 

5 Important Homonyms

1. Stationary (स्थिर): not moving; fixed in one place

2. Stationery (लेखन सामग्री): writing materials such as paper and pens

3. Complement (पूरक): something that completes or makes perfect

4. Compliment (प्रशंसा): a polite expression of praise or admiration

5. Council (परिषद): a group of people who advise or govern

question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the following sentence:

 

Thick fog began to ______ the entire valley by early morning.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Envelop.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Envelop means to cover or wrap something completely (verb). (ढक लेना)
◦ Example: Darkness slowly began to envelop the small village as the sun set.

 

• The sentence is correctly completed with Envelop: "Thick fog began to Envelop the entire valley by early morning."

 

• Remember the stress and part of speech: Envelop (verb, stress on the second syllable) means to cover, while Envelope (noun, stress on the first syllable) is the paper cover for a letter.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Envelope (लिफाफा): a paper covering used to enclose a letter.

 

• Option 3: Envisage (कल्पना करना): to imagine or foresee as a future possibility.

 

• Option 4: Envoy (दूत): a diplomatic messenger or representative.

 

NOTE

 

• Other pairs frequently tested by SSC: Advice/Advise, Device/Devise, and Loose/Lose.

 

5 Important Homonyms

1. Advice (सलाह): a suggestion given to help someone (noun)

2. Advise (सलाह देना): to give a suggestion or recommendation (verb)

3. Device (उपकरण): a machine or tool made for a purpose (noun)

4. Devise (तैयार करना): to plan or invent something (verb)

5. Loose (ढीला): not firmly fixed; not tight

question:
Select the sentence containing the homonym of the highlighted and underline word:

 

The Archbishop received the pallium from the Pope during a solemn ceremony in Rome.
option_1: The newly appointed cardinal wore a pallium made of white wool with black crosses.
option_2: In vertebrate brains, the pallium forms the outer layer that gives rise to the cerebral cortex.
option_3: Each pallium is traditionally woven from the wool of lambs blessed on a special feast day.
option_4: The Pope personally bestowed the pallium upon several metropolitan archbishops that year.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. In vertebrate brains, the pallium forms the outer layer that gives rise to the cerebral cortex.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A homonym is a word with the same spelling and pronunciation but a wholly different meaning. In the given sentence, Pallium means a woollen vestment worn by senior Catholic clergy. (धार्मिक वस्त्र)

 

• In Option 2, Pallium is a term used in neuroanatomy — the outer layer of the brain forming the cerebral cortex. (मस्तिष्क का आवरण) That is an entirely different sense, and therefore the homonym required.

 

• Both senses share the same Latin root pallium, meaning 'cloak' or 'covering' — the brain's pallium is so named because it cloaks the deeper structures of the brain, just as the vestment cloaks the shoulders.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 uses Pallium in the same sense as the question — a woollen vestment worn by senior Catholic clergy: "The newly appointed cardinal wore a pallium made of white wool with black crosses."

 

• Option 3 again uses Pallium to mean a woollen vestment worn by senior Catholic clergy: "Each pallium is traditionally woven from the wool of lambs blessed on a special feast day."

 

• Option 4 likewise uses Pallium in its primary sense (a woollen vestment worn by senior Catholic clergy): "The Pope personally bestowed the pallium upon several metropolitan archbishops that year."

 

NOTE

 

• This word shows how homonyms sometimes arise from one original meaning branching into a technical field — similar to how cell came to mean both a small room and a biological unit.

 

5 Important Homonyms

1. Cell (कोशिका / कोठरी): a biological unit; also, a small prison room

2. Trunk (तना / संदूक): the main stem of a tree; also, a large storage box

3. Palm (हथेली / ताड़ का पेड़): the inner surface of the hand; also, a tropical tree

4. Fan (पंखा / प्रशंसक): a device that creates a cooling breeze; also, an enthusiastic supporter

5. Racket (रैकेट / शोर): a bat used in tennis or badminton; also, a loud disturbing noise

question:
Select the sentence containing the homonym of the highlighted and underline word:

 

A severe storm battered the coastal villages throughout the night.
option_1: Meteorologists warned that a powerful storm was approaching the eastern coastline.
option_2: The old fisherman refused to sail out to sea because of the coming storm.
option_3: Flights were cancelled across the region due to the unexpected storm.
option_4: Special forces were ordered to storm the building and rescue the hostages.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Special forces were ordered to storm the building and rescue the hostages.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A homonym is a word with the same spelling and pronunciation but a wholly different meaning. In the given sentence, Storm means a violent disturbance of weather with strong winds. (तूफान)

 

• In Option 4, Storm is a military verb meaning to assault — to attack or capture a place suddenly by force. (ज़ोरदार हमला) That is an entirely different sense, and therefore the homonym required.

 

• The idiom 'to storm out of a room' uses yet another shade of this sense — moving abruptly in anger, which shows sudden forceful action rather than actual violence.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 uses Storm in the same sense as the question — a violent disturbance of weather with strong winds: "Meteorologists warned that a powerful storm was approaching the eastern coastline."

 

• Option 2 again uses Storm to mean a violent disturbance of weather with strong winds: "The old fisherman refused to sail out to sea because of the coming storm."

 

• Option 3 likewise uses Storm in its primary sense (a violent disturbance of weather with strong winds): "Flights were cancelled across the region due to the unexpected storm."

 

NOTE

 

• Homonyms often extend from a literal meaning to a figurative one, as seen here — the violence of a weather storm gave rise to the idea of a sudden forceful attack.

 

5 Important Homonyms

1. Rock (चट्टान / झुलाना): a large stone; also, to move gently back and forth

2. Season (मौसम / मसाला डालना): a period of the year; also, to add flavour to food

3. Mint (पुदीना / टकसाल): an aromatic herb; also, a place where coins are made

4. Spring (वसंत / झरना / कूदना): a season; also, a water source; also, to jump suddenly

5. Row (पंक्ति / झगड़ा): a line of things; also, a noisy argument

question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the following sentence:

 

The professor asked students to ______ at least three credible sources in their research paper.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Cite.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Cite means to quote or refer to as evidence or example. (उद्धृत करना)
◦ Example: The lawyer will cite a previous court ruling to support her argument.

 

• The sentence is correctly completed with Cite: "The professor asked students to Cite at least three credible sources in their research paper."

 

• This trio is one of the most frequently tested homophone sets in SSC exams — Cite (quote), Site (place), and Sight (vision) are pronounced identically but never interchangeable.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Site (स्थान): a particular place where something is located or will be built.

 

• Option 2: Sight (दृष्टि): the ability to see; also, something seen.

 

• Option 3: Incite (उकसाना): to encourage or stir someone into violent or unlawful action.

 

NOTE

 

• Similar homophone trios include Right/Write/Rite and Made/Maid.

 

5 Important Homonyms

1. Right (सही / अधिकार): correct; also, a moral or legal entitlement

2. Write (लिखना): to form letters or words on a surface

3. Rite (धार्मिक संस्कार): a religious or solemn ceremony

4. Made (बनाया): past tense of make; created or produced

5. Maid (नौकरानी): a female domestic servant

question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the following sentence:

 

The manager tried to ______ the anxious clients that their orders would be delivered on time.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Assure.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assure means to tell someone confidently that something is true, to remove doubt. (आश्वस्त करना)
◦ Example: I can assure you that all necessary precautions have been taken.

 

• The sentence is correctly completed with Assure: "The manager tried to Assure the anxious clients that their orders would be delivered on time."

 

• Memory trick: Assure a person, Ensure a result, Insure your property — each verb takes a different kind of object.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Ensure (सुनिश्चित करना): to make certain that something will happen.

 

• Option 3: Insure (बीमा करना): to arrange compensation in the event of loss or damage.

 

• Option 4: Assurance (आश्वासन): a positive declaration intended to give confidence (noun).

 

NOTE

 

• Other commonly confused sets tested by SSC: Emigrate/Immigrate/Migrate, Continual/Continuous, and Historic/Historical.

 

5 Important Homonyms

1. Emigrate (देश से बाहर जाना): to leave one's own country to settle in another

2. Immigrate (देश में आकर बसना): to come into a foreign country to live permanently

3. Migrate (प्रवास करना): to move from one place to another, often seasonally

4. Continuous (निरंतर): happening without any interruption or break

5. Historic (ऐतिहासिक महत्व का): famous or important in history

question:
Select the sentence containing the homonym of the highlighted and underline word:

 

His ankle began to swell painfully after he twisted it on the stairs.
option_1: That's a real swell idea — let's do it this weekend!
option_2: The river began to swell rapidly after three days of continuous rain.
option_3: Her fingers started to swell due to the bee sting.
option_4: The crowd outside the stadium continued to swell as kick-off approached.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. That's a real swell idea — let's do it this weekend!

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A homonym is a word with the same spelling and pronunciation but a wholly different meaning. In the given sentence, Swell means to increase in size, volume, or intensity. (सूजना / बढ़ना)

 

• In Option 1, Swell is an old-fashioned slang adjective — excellent or wonderful (informal, dated usage). (बहुत बढ़िया) That is an entirely different sense, and therefore the homonym required.

 

• This slang sense of swell was especially popular in early-to-mid 20th-century American English and now sounds distinctly old-fashioned.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 uses Swell in the same sense as the question — to increase in size, volume, or intensity: "The river began to swell rapidly after three days of continuous rain."

 

• Option 3 again uses Swell to mean to increase in size, volume, or intensity: "Her fingers started to swell due to the bee sting."

 

• Option 4 likewise uses Swell in its primary sense (to increase in size, volume, or intensity): "The crowd outside the stadium continued to swell as kick-off approached."

 

NOTE

 

• Not all homonyms are equally common today — some senses, like this slang use of swell, have faded from everyday speech but may still appear in older texts or exams testing vocabulary depth.

 

5 Important Homonyms

1. Mean (मतलब होना / कंजूस): to signify something; also, unkind or unwilling to give

2. Fine (जुर्माना / बढ़िया): a monetary penalty; also, of high quality

3. Fast (तेज़ / उपवास करना): quick in speed; also, to abstain from food

4. Well (कुआं / अच्छी तरह से): a hole dug for water; also, in a good or thorough manner

5. Tender (कोमल / निविदा): soft and gentle; also, a formal offer to supply goods or services

question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the following sentence:

 

The new library will serve as the cultural ______ of the town.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Centre.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Centre means the middle point or main hub of something (British spelling). (केंद्र)
◦ Example: Please move the vase to the centre of the table.

 

• The sentence is correctly completed with Centre: "The new library will serve as the cultural Centre of the town."

 

• SSC and most competitive exams in India follow British spelling conventions, so Centre is correct while the American spelling Center is marked wrong, just like Colour/Color and Theatre/Theater.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Center (केंद्र): the American English spelling of the same word.

 

• Option 2: Central (केंद्रीय): an adjective meaning located at or forming the centre.

 

• Option 3: Centrist (मध्यमार्गी): a person who holds moderate political views.

 

NOTE

 

• Other British-American spelling pairs to remember: Colour/Color, Programme/Program, and Realise/Realize.

 

5 Important Homonyms

1. Colour (रंग): the British spelling of 'color'

2. Programme (कार्यक्रम): the British spelling of 'program' (a plan or schedule)

3. Realise (एहसास करना): the British spelling of 'realize' (to become aware)

4. Metre (मीटर): the British spelling of 'meter' (a unit of length)

5. Labour (श्रम): the British spelling of 'labor' (work or workers)

question:
Select the sentence containing the homonym of the highlighted and underline word:

 

The company launched a new compact camera that fits easily into a pocket.
option_1: This compact refrigerator is perfect for a small apartment.
option_2: The manufacturer introduced a compact and lightweight laptop for students.
option_3: Her handbag contained a compact umbrella that folded neatly into her palm.
option_4: The two neighbouring countries signed a compact to share river water resources.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The two neighbouring countries signed a compact to share river water resources.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A homonym is a word with the same spelling and pronunciation but a wholly different meaning. In the given sentence, Compact means small and conveniently sized; taking up little space. (छोटा उपकरण)

 

• In Option 4, Compact is a legal or political term for an agreement — a formal agreement or pact between parties. (समझौता) That is an entirely different sense, and therefore the homonym required.

 

• Both senses trace back to Latin compactus ('packed together') — one meaning 'closely packed, small', the other 'an agreement reached together'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 uses Compact in the same sense as the question — small and conveniently sized; taking up little space: "This compact refrigerator is perfect for a small apartment."

 

• Option 2 again uses Compact to mean small and conveniently sized; taking up little space: "The manufacturer introduced a compact and lightweight laptop for students."

 

• Option 3 likewise uses Compact in its primary sense (small and conveniently sized; taking up little space): "Her handbag contained a compact umbrella that folded neatly into her palm."

 

NOTE

 

• Compare with other true homonyms like Novel (a book / new and original) and Second (next after first / a unit of time).

 

5 Important Homonyms

1. Novel (उपन्यास / नया): a long fictional book; also, new and original

2. Second (सेकंड / दूसरा): a unit of time; also, coming after the first

3. Present (उपहार / वर्तमान): a gift; also, the current time or being there

4. Ring (अंगूठी / बजना): a piece of jewellery; also, to make a bell sound

5. Bank (बैंक / नदी का किनारा): a financial institution; also, the side of a river

question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the following sentence:

 

The bank sent an expert to ______ the property before approving the loan.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Appraise.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Appraise means to assess the value or quality of something. (मूल्यांकन करना)
◦ Example: The manager will appraise each employee's performance at the end of the year.

 

• The sentence is correctly completed with Appraise: "The bank sent an expert to Appraise the property before approving the loan."

 

• Appraise (to evaluate) has two A's, like 'Assess the vAlue'; Apprise (to inform) can be linked to 'wise' — being apprised makes you wise about the facts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Apprise (सूचित करना): to inform or notify someone about something.

 

• Option 2: Praise (प्रशंसा करना): to express warm approval or admiration.

 

• Option 4: Reprise (पुनरावृत्ति): a repetition or resumption of something, especially in music.

 

NOTE

 

• Other pairs SSC frequently tests: Elicit/Illicit, Adapt/Adopt/Adept, and Stationary/Stationery.

 

5 Important Homonyms

1. Elicit (निकलवाना): to draw out a response or fact from someone

2. Illicit (अवैध): not legally permitted; forbidden by law

3. Adapt (अनुकूल बनना): to adjust to new conditions

4. Adopt (अपनाना): to take up and use as one's own

5. Adept (कुशल): very skilled at something

question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the following sentence:

 

The state government promulgated a new ______ to regulate street vending.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Ordinance.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ordinance means an authoritative order or decree having force of law. (अध्यादेश)
◦ Example: The municipal corporation passed an ordinance banning single-use plastics.

 

• The sentence is correctly completed with Ordinance: "The state government promulgated a new Ordinance to regulate street vending."

 

• Note the spelling difference: Ordinance (a law) has an extra 'i', while Ordnance (weapons) drops it — think 'i' for 'issued law'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Ordnance (हथियार सामग्री): military weapons, ammunition, and equipment.

 

• Option 3: Ordinary (साधारण): commonplace or usual; not special.

 

• Option 4: Ordination (नियुक्ति संस्कार): the act of formally appointing someone as clergy.

 

NOTE

 

• Other confusable pairs frequently tested: Complement/Compliment, Council/Counsel, and Desert/Dessert.

 

5 Important Homonyms

1. Counsel (सलाह देना): advice, especially formal or legal; also, to advise

2. Desert (रेगिस्तान / त्याग देना): a dry, arid region; also, to abandon someone

3. Dessert (मिठाई): a sweet course served at the end of a meal

4. Human (मानव): relating to or characteristic of people

5. Humane (दयालु): having compassion or benevolence

question:
Select the sentence containing the homonym of the highlighted and underline word:

 

The judge ensured a fair trial for both parties involved in the case.
option_1: It is only fair that everyone gets an equal share of the profit.
option_2: The referee was praised for making fair decisions throughout the match.
option_3: Employers must offer a fair wage to all their workers.
option_4: The poem describes the fair maiden standing beside the flowing river.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The poem describes the fair maiden standing beside the flowing river.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A homonym is a word with the same spelling and pronunciation but a wholly different meaning. In the given sentence, Fair means just, reasonable, and free from bias. (उचित / मेला)

 

• In Option 4, Fair is an old-fashioned adjective for beauty — beautiful or lovely in appearance, especially of a woman. (किराया / Fair – न्यायसंगत) That is an entirely different sense, and therefore the homonym required.

 

• Fair also has a third common sense — a mela or exhibition, as in 'a book fair' — and should not be confused with its homophone Fare (किराया), meaning the cost of a journey or food served.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 uses Fair in the same sense as the question — just, reasonable, and free from bias: "It is only fair that everyone gets an equal share of the profit."

 

• Option 2 again uses Fair to mean just, reasonable, and free from bias: "The referee was praised for making fair decisions throughout the match."

 

• Option 3 likewise uses Fair in its primary sense (just, reasonable, and free from bias): "Employers must offer a fair wage to all their workers."

 

NOTE

 

• Homophones like Fair/Fare sound identical but are spelled differently and carry unrelated meanings, unlike true homonyms such as Fair (just) and Fair (beautiful), which share one spelling.

 

5 Important Homonyms

1. Yard (गज़ / आंगन): a unit of length; also, an enclosed outdoor area

2. Scale (तराजू / पैमाना): a device for weighing; also, a graded system of measurement

3. Pupil (छात्र / पुतली): a student; also, the black centre of the eye

4. Match (माचिस / प्रतियोगिता): a small stick for lighting fire; also, a sports contest

5. Sound (ध्वनि / स्वस्थ): noise that can be heard; also, healthy or in good condition

question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the following sentence:

 

It is difficult to ______ the scorching heat of the desert without water.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Bear.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bear means a large wild animal; also, to endure or tolerate. (भालू / सहन करना)
◦ Example: You must bear the consequences of your own actions.

 

• The sentence is correctly completed with Bear: "It is difficult to Bear the scorching heat of the desert without water."

 

• SSC frequently tests the full Bear-Bore-Born/Borne verb-form set: 'The tree has borne fruit' vs 'She was born in Delhi' — note the different past participles for different meanings of bear.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Bare (नग्न / बिना ढके): uncovered, plain, or without covering.

 

• Option 3: Boar (जंगली सूअर): a wild male pig.

 

• Option 4: Bore (छेद करना / उबाना): to drill a hole; or, to make someone feel dull and tired.

 

NOTE

 

• Other homophone-style confusable sets tested by SSC include Break/Brake, Meet/Meat, and Rain/Reign.

 

5 Important Homonyms

1. Break (तोड़ना): to separate into pieces by force

2. Brake (ब्रेक): a device used to slow or stop a vehicle

3. Meet (मिलना): to come together with someone

4. Meat (मांस): the flesh of an animal used as food

5. Reign (शासन करना): the period during which a monarch rules

question:
Select the sentence containing the homonym of the highlighted and underline word:

 

She achieved a First Class in the Mathematical Tripos at Cambridge University.
option_1: Many students consider the Natural Sciences Tripos to be extremely demanding.
option_2: In earlier centuries, the examiner would sit upon a wooden tripos to question the candidates aloud.
option_3: The results of this year's Tripos examinations were declared last week.
option_4: He spent three years preparing rigorously for the Classics Tripos.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. In earlier centuries, the examiner would sit upon a wooden tripos to question the candidates aloud.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A homonym is a word with the same spelling and pronunciation but a wholly different meaning. In the given sentence, Tripos means the honours examination system at Cambridge University. (परीक्षा प्रणाली)

 

• In Option 2, Tripos is an archaic furniture term — an old three-legged stool or table. (तिपाई) That is an entirely different sense, and therefore the homonym required.

 

• The word comes from Greek tripous, meaning 'three-footed' — the examination sense developed because candidates were once questioned while seated on this very three-legged stool.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 uses Tripos in the same sense as the question — the honours examination system at Cambridge University: "Many students consider the Natural Sciences Tripos to be extremely demanding."

 

• Option 3 again uses Tripos to mean the honours examination system at Cambridge University: "The results of this year's Tripos examinations were declared last week."

 

• Option 4 likewise uses Tripos in its primary sense (the honours examination system at Cambridge University): "He spent three years preparing rigorously for the Classics Tripos."

 

NOTE

 

• This is a rare example of a word whose modern meaning grew directly out of its older, literal meaning — compare how clerk once meant only a clergyman before coming to mean an office worker.

 

5 Important Homonyms

1. Content (संतुष्ट / विषय-वस्तु): satisfied; also, the material contained within something

2. Object (वस्तु / आपत्ति करना): a physical thing; also, to express disapproval

3. Produce (उत्पादन करना / उपज): to make or create; also, fresh farm goods

4. Digest (पचाना / सार-संग्रह): to break down food in the body; also, a summary of information

5. Grave (कब्र / गंभीर): a burial site; also, serious or solemn

question:
Select the sentence containing the homonym of the highlighted and underline word:

 

The sailors gathered on the deck to watch the sunset over the ocean.
option_1: Passengers were advised to remain below deck during the storm.
option_2: He shuffled the deck of cards before dealing them to the players.
option_3: The captain inspected every deck of the massive cruise ship.
option_4: Children played happily on the sunny upper deck of the ferry.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. He shuffled the deck of cards before dealing them to the players.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A homonym is a word with the same spelling and pronunciation but a wholly different meaning. In the given sentence, Deck means the floor-like platform of a ship. (जहाज़ का फर्श)

 

• In Option 2, Deck is a term used in card games — a complete pack of playing cards. (ताश के पत्ते) That is an entirely different sense, and therefore the homonym required.

 

• Deck can also be used as a verb meaning 'to decorate', as in the carol line 'Deck the halls with boughs of holly.'

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 uses Deck in the same sense as the question — the floor-like platform of a ship: "Passengers were advised to remain below deck during the storm."

 

• Option 3 again uses Deck to mean the floor-like platform of a ship: "The captain inspected every deck of the massive cruise ship."

 

• Option 4 likewise uses Deck in its primary sense (the floor-like platform of a ship): "Children played happily on the sunny upper deck of the ferry."

 

NOTE

 

• Compare with other true homonyms such as Bat (flying mammal / sports equipment) and Watch (a timepiece / to observe).

 

5 Important Homonyms

1. Ring (अंगूठी / बजना): a piece of jewellery; also, to make a bell sound

2. Bat (चमगादड़ / बल्ला): a flying mammal; also, sports equipment

3. Watch (घड़ी / देखना): a small timepiece; also, to observe something

4. Cricket (झींगुर / क्रिकेट खेल): a chirping insect; also, a popular bat-and-ball sport

5. Nail (नाखून / कील): the hard covering on a fingertip; also, a metal spike

question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the following sentence:

 

The two colleagues developed an ______ friendship over the years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Intimate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Intimate means very close, personal, and familiar in nature. (घनिष्ठ)
◦ Example: They shared an intimate bond built on years of mutual trust.

 

• The sentence is correctly completed with Intimate: "The two colleagues developed an Intimate friendship over the years."

 

• Watch the extra syllable: Intimidate (to frighten) has one more syllable than Intimate (close/personal) — say them aloud slowly to hear the difference.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Imitate (नकल करना): to copy the behaviour or actions of someone.

 

• Option 2: Intimidate (डराना): to frighten or threaten someone.

 

• Option 4: Intimation (सूचना): a formal notice or indirect hint.

 

NOTE

 

• Other look-alike pairs SSC tests often: Eligible/Illegible, Alternate/Alternative, and Adverse/Averse.

 

5 Important Homonyms

1. Eligible (योग्य): having the right to be chosen or to do something

2. Illegible (अपठनीय): not clear enough to be read

3. Alternate (बारी-बारी से): occurring in turns; every other one

4. Alternative (विकल्प): another possible choice or option

5. Adverse (प्रतिकूल): unfavourable or harmful in effect

question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the following sentence:

 

Regular ______ is essential if you want to master a musical instrument.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Practice.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Practice means repeated exercise carried out to improve a skill (noun). (अभ्यास)
◦ Example: Good dental practice recommends brushing your teeth twice a day.

 

• The sentence is correctly completed with Practice: "Regular Practice is essential if you want to master a musical instrument."

 

• Remember: Practice is the noun ('ice' is nice, a thing), while Practise is the verb ('ise' is an action) — this mirrors the Licence/License and Advice/Advise pattern.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Practise (अभ्यास करना): to perform an activity repeatedly to improve a skill (verb).

 

• Option 2: Practical (व्यावहारिक): relating to real actions rather than ideas or theories.

 

• Option 4: Practitioner (व्यवसायी): a person who practises a profession, especially medicine.

 

NOTE

 

• Other noun-verb spelling pairs tested by SSC: Licence/License, Advice/Advise, and Device/Devise.

 

5 Important Homonyms

1. Licence (अनुज्ञापत्र): an official permit (noun, British spelling)

2. License (अनुमति देना): to grant official permission (verb, British spelling)

3. Prophecy (भविष्यवाणी): a prediction of the future (noun)

4. Prophesy (भविष्यवाणी करना): to predict the future (verb)

5. Breath (सांस): the air taken into or let out of the lungs (noun)

question:
Select the sentence containing the homonym of the highlighted and underline word:

 

Medieval foot soldiers often carried a long pike to fend off cavalry charges.
option_1: The angler proudly displayed the large pike he had caught in the lake.
option_2: The museum displayed an ancient pike used by infantry soldiers centuries ago.
option_3: Historians say the pike was eventually replaced by the bayonet on the battlefield.
option_4: Soldiers were trained to form a defensive wall using long pikes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The angler proudly displayed the large pike he had caught in the lake.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A homonym is a word with the same spelling and pronunciation but a wholly different meaning. In the given sentence, Pike means a long spear used by foot soldiers. (भाला)

 

• In Option 1, Pike is a type of fish — a large freshwater fish with a pointed snout. (मछली) That is an entirely different sense, and therefore the homonym required.

 

• In British English, pike can also refer to a mountain peak, as seen in place names like 'Scafell Pike'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 uses Pike in the same sense as the question — a long spear used by foot soldiers: "The museum displayed an ancient pike used by infantry soldiers centuries ago."

 

• Option 3 again uses Pike to mean a long spear used by foot soldiers: "Historians say the pike was eventually replaced by the bayonet on the battlefield."

 

• Option 4 likewise uses Pike in its primary sense (a long spear used by foot soldiers): "Soldiers were trained to form a defensive wall using long pikes."

 

NOTE

 

• True homonyms like pike differ from confusable pairs such as Peak/Peek/Pique, which sound alike but are spelled differently.

 

5 Important Homonyms

1. Peak (चोटी): the pointed top of a mountain; the highest point

2. Peek (झांकना): to look quickly and often secretively

3. Pique (चिढ़ / उत्सुकता जगाना): a feeling of irritation; also, to arouse curiosity

4. Sole (तलवा / अकेला / एक मछली): the bottom of a foot or shoe; also, the only one; also, a flatfish

5. Seam (सिलाई की रेखा): a line where two pieces of fabric are sewn together

question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the following sentence:

 

The jeweller certified the diamond as a flawless two-______ stone.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Carat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Carat means a unit of weight used for gemstones such as diamonds. (रत्न का भार)
◦ Example: The engagement ring featured a brilliant one-carat diamond.

 

• The sentence is correctly completed with Carat: "The jeweller certified the diamond as a flawless two-Carat stone."

 

• SSC often tests this exact four-way set together: Carat (gem weight), Caret (proofreading mark), Karat (gold purity), and Carrot (vegetable) — all pronounced almost identically.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Caret (सुधार चिह्न): a proofreading mark (^) showing where to insert text.

 

• Option 2: Karat (सोने की शुद्धता): a unit measuring the purity of gold.

 

• Option 4: Carrot (गाजर): an orange root vegetable.

 

NOTE

 

• Similar homophone quartets include Rain/Rein and To/Too/Two.

 

5 Important Homonyms

1. Rain (बारिश): water falling from clouds

2. Rein (लगाम): a strap used to control a horse

3. To (तक / की ओर): a preposition indicating direction or purpose

4. Too (भी / बहुत): also; or, to an excessive degree

5. Two (दो): the number 2

question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the following sentence:

 

The ______ to the summit took the climbers nearly six exhausting hours.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Ascent.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ascent means the act of climbing or rising upward. (चढ़ाई)
◦ Example: The pilot reported a smooth ascent through the clouds.

 

• The sentence is correctly completed with Ascent: "The Ascent to the summit took the climbers nearly six exhausting hours."

 

• Remember: Ascent (a climb) is a noun ending in '-cent' like 'rising'; Assent (agreement) has a double 's' like 'say yes'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Assent (सहमति): agreement or approval expressed formally.

 

• Option 3: Accent (उच्चारण): a distinctive manner of pronunciation.

 

• Option 4: Ascend (चढ़ना): to move upward or climb (verb form).

 

NOTE

 

• Other tricky pairs: Descent/Dissent, Access/Excess, and Accept/Except.

 

5 Important Homonyms

1. Descent (अवतरण): the act of moving downward

2. Dissent (असहमति): disagreement with an official view or decision

3. Access (पहुंच): the means or opportunity to approach or enter

4. Excess (अतिरिक्त): an amount that is more than necessary

5. Latter (बाद वाला): referring to the second of two things mentioned

question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the following sentence:

 

Skilled manpower is regarded as an important economic ______ that drives national growth.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Resource.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Resource means a supply or source of wealth, support, or aid. (संसाधन)
◦ Example: Human resource management focuses on hiring and training employees effectively.

 

• The sentence is correctly completed with Resource: "Skilled manpower is regarded as an important economic Resource that drives national growth."

 

• Recourse is almost always followed by 'to', as in 'without recourse to violence', while Resource stands alone as a noun for supplies or assets.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Recourse (सहारा): a source of help in a difficult situation.

 

• Option 2: Resourceful (साधन-संपन्न): good at finding quick and clever solutions to problems.

 

• Option 4: Reserve (आरक्षित भंडार): a supply of something kept back for future use.

 

NOTE

 

• Other pairs frequently tested: Course/Coarse, Source/Sauce, and Precede/Proceed.

 

5 Important Homonyms

1. Course (पाठ्यक्रम / मार्ग): a series of studies; also, a direction or route

2. Coarse (खुरदरा): rough or harsh in texture

3. Source (स्रोत): a place or thing from which something originates

4. Precede (पहले होना): to come before something in time or order

5. Proceed (आगे बढ़ना): to continue or go forward with an action

question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the following sentence:

 

The film's ______ battle scene left the entire audience on the edge of their seats.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Climactic.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Climactic means relating to the most intense or decisive point (climax). (चरम से संबंधित)
◦ Example: The novel builds steadily toward its climactic final chapter.

 

• The sentence is correctly completed with Climactic: "The film's Climactic battle scene left the entire audience on the edge of their seats."

 

• Climactic relates to a climax (peak moment), while Climatic relates to climate (weather) — matching each adjective to the noun it comes from helps avoid confusion.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Climatic (जलवायु संबंधी): relating to climate or weather patterns.

 

• Option 3: Climate (जलवायु): the general weather conditions of an area over a long period.

 

• Option 4: Climax (चरम बिंदु): the most intense or important point of a story or event.

 

NOTE

 

• Similarly confused pairs: Economic/Economical, Historic/Historical, and Continual/Continuous.

 

5 Important Homonyms

1. Economic (आर्थिक): relating to the economy or trade

2. Economical (मितव्ययी): careful with money or resources; cost-effective

3. Historic (ऐतिहासिक महत्व का): famous or important in history

4. Historical (इतिहास से संबंधित): relating to history in general

5. Continual (बार-बार होने वाला): happening frequently with breaks in between

question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the following sentence:

 

It would be ______ to argue with someone who refuses to listen to reason.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Vain.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vain means having excessive pride; or, useless and without result. (घमंडी / व्यर्थ)
◦ Example: He was too vain to admit that he had made a mistake.

 

• The sentence is correctly completed with Vain: "It would be Vain to argue with someone who refuses to listen to reason."

 

• SSC loves this exact homophone quartet — Vain (proud/useless), Vein (blood vessel), Vane (wind indicator), and Vine (climbing plant) — all sound alike but mean completely different things.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Vein (नस): a blood vessel carrying blood toward the heart.

 

• Option 3: Vane (दिशा सूचक): a device that shows the direction of the wind.

 

• Option 4: Vine (बेल): a climbing or trailing plant, often bearing grapes.

 

NOTE

 

• Compare with other homophone sets: Bridal/Bridle, Cellar/Seller, and Currant/Current.

 

5 Important Homonyms

1. Bridal (दुल्हन संबंधी): relating to a bride or a wedding

2. Bridle (लगाम): a harness used to control a horse's head

3. Cellar (तहखाना): an underground room used for storage

4. Seller (विक्रेता): a person who sells something

5. Currant (किशमिश जैसा फल): a small dried fruit or berry

question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the following sentence:

 

She would often ______ over old manuscripts late into the night at the library.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Pore.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pore means to read or study something with great attention. (ध्यान से पढ़ना)
◦ Example: Scientists pore over the data for hours before publishing their findings.

 

• The sentence is correctly completed with Pore: "She would often Pore over old manuscripts late into the night at the library."

 

• Pore as a noun also means a tiny opening in the skin, as in 'sweat escapes through the pores' — context decides whether it is a verb (to study closely) or a noun (skin opening).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Pour (डालना): to cause liquid to flow from a container.

 

• Option 2: Poor (गरीब): having little money or means; lacking in something.

 

• Option 3: Paw (पंजा): the foot of an animal that has claws or nails.

 

NOTE

 

• Other homophone sets tested by SSC: Flower/Flour, Mail/Male, and Waist/Waste.

 

5 Important Homonyms

1. Flower (फूल): the colourful reproductive part of a plant

2. Flour (आटा): a powder made from ground grain, used in baking

3. Mail (डाक): letters and packages sent through the postal system

4. Male (पुरुष): of the sex that does not bear offspring; a man

5. Waist (कमर): the narrow part of the body between ribs and hips

question:
Select the sentence containing the homonym of the highlighted and underline word:

 

Please bring an extra chair for the guest who just arrived.
option_1: The old wooden chair creaked loudly whenever someone sat on it.
option_2: He pulled up a chair and joined the discussion at the table.
option_3: Dr. Sharma will chair tomorrow's meeting of the college academic council.
option_4: The office ordered fifty new ergonomic chairs for the staff.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Dr. Sharma will chair tomorrow's meeting of the college academic council.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A homonym is a word with the same spelling and pronunciation but a wholly different meaning. In the given sentence, Chair means a piece of furniture for one person to sit on. (कुर्सी)

 

• In Option 3, Chair is a verb meaning to preside — to preside over or lead a meeting or committee. (अध्यक्षता करना) That is an entirely different sense, and therefore the homonym required.

 

• Chair can also refer to a position of authority, as in 'the chair of the department', or historically to a throne (सिंहासन) occupied by a king or high official.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 uses Chair in the same sense as the question — a piece of furniture for one person to sit on: "The old wooden chair creaked loudly whenever someone sat on it."

 

• Option 2 again uses Chair to mean a piece of furniture for one person to sit on: "He pulled up a chair and joined the discussion at the table."

 

• Option 4 likewise uses Chair in its primary sense (a piece of furniture for one person to sit on): "The office ordered fifty new ergonomic chairs for the staff."

 

NOTE

 

• This is a classic example of a noun functioning as a verb through a shift in usage — compare table (furniture / to table a motion) and book (a reading item / to book a ticket).

 

5 Important Homonyms

1. Table (मेज़ / प्रस्तुत करना): a piece of furniture; also, to formally propose a motion

2. Book (किताब / आरक्षित करना): a written work to read; also, to reserve something in advance

3. Bill (बिल / विधेयक): a statement of money owed; also, a proposed law

4. Duty (कर्तव्य / शुल्क): a moral obligation; also, a tax on goods

5. Bolt (कुंडी / भाग जाना): a metal fastening pin; also, to run away suddenly
